New plan: 

Upon reflection, I realize that I failed to identify the formal fallacies in the arguments. In particular, I did not recognize the invalidity of the third argument. To improve my strategy, I will focus on carefully analyzing the premises and the conclusion of each argument, looking for any logical flaws or inconsistencies. I will also pay closer attention to the use of quantifiers (e.g., "every," "some," "all") and the relationships between the different statements. Specifically, I will ask myself questions like: "Does the conclusion logically follow from the premises?" "Are there any implicit assumptions or unstated premises that could affect the validity of the argument?" "Are there any logical fallacies, such as affirming the consequent or denying the antecedent?" By asking these questions and carefully examining the arguments, I hope to improve my ability to distinguish deductively valid arguments from formal fallacies.
